title: The Determinant of a Square Matrix

cards.front: What is the determinant of a $2 \times 2$ matrix $\begin{bmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{bmatrix}$?
If the determinant of a square matrix is zero, what does that indicate?
cards.back: The matrix is singular and does not have an inverse.

cards.front: What is a minor $M_{ij}$ of a matrix?
cards.back: The determinant of the submatrix formed by deleting the $i$th row and $j$th column.

cards.front: Describe the sign pattern for cofactors in a $3 \times 3$ matrix.
cards.back: Checkerboard: (+, -, +) in first row, (-, +, -) in second, (+, -, +) in third. Formally, positive if $i+j$ even, negative if odd.

cards.front: How do you compute the determinant of a $3 \times 3$ matrix using cofactors?
cards.back: Expand along a row (or column): $\det(A) = a_{i1}C_{i1} + a_{i2}C_{i2} + a_{i3}C_{i3}$ for row $i$.

cards.front: Why is it useful to expand along a row or column with many zeros?
cards.back: Zero entries times their cofactors equal zero, so fewer cofactors need to be computed, simplifying the calculation.

cards.front: For a $3 \times 3$ matrix, how many cofactors must be computed if you expand along a row with no zeros?
What is the determinant of a $1 \times 1$ matrix $[a]$?
In the cofactor expansion, if a row has a single nonzero entry $a_{ij}$, what is the determinant?
What is the determinant of a triangular matrix?
cards.back: The product of the entries on the main diagonal.

cards.front: If you interchange two rows of a matrix, what happens to the determinant?
cards.back: The sign of the determinant changes.
